newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound vs dollar, seen testing 2.5250.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound vs dollar, seen testing 2.5250.

text.p: The ringgit was kept in a tight range against the dollar in Asian trading on Thursday, but dealers said ringgit sentiment was still weak and the dollar might test higher levels again.
"Dollar/ringgit may try for the 2.5250 level again later today or tomorrow," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "The dollar is still well bid by offshore players."
Dealers said the dollar/ringgit was sandwiched by profit-taking and local corporate selling around 2.5240 and offshore buying around 2.5200.
At 1000 GMT, ringgit was quoted at 2.5207/17 a dollar. It closed at 2.5232/42 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Dollar gains were again capped by fears of central bank intervention, dealers said.
Although there was no sign of Bank Negara's presence, dealers believed the central bank was monitoring the situation.
Dealers said offshore bids for the dollar would continue to keep ringgit defensive. They said dollar demand was prompted by mid-year book closing and some window-dressing activities.

Dealers said dollar/ringgit also maintained its positive bias after a widely expected Bank Negara lending maturity on Thursday, said to be for two billion ringgit, failed to materialise. Interbank rates continued to fall on Thursday as the market remained flush.
